punchline: A weight on a nail in a hand overturned a picture painters had repeated for centuries.
thirty_sec: French surgeon Pierre Barbet nailed freshly amputated hands and found the skin between the fingers tore at about 88 pounds of pull, so he proposed the wrist instead. Decades later Frederick Zugibe's own cadaver tests contradicted parts of Barbet's conclusions.
question: Which assumption at your work has been repeated for years without a real test?
key_contrast: A shared picture against a measured pull.
